title: Executive Engage One-Pager: Quarterly Outcomes & Renewal Pulse
body:
Purpose:
This is a compact, single-page template for an executive sponsor touchpoint and a short customer-facing quarterly digest. Built for 10–15 minute check-ins with an exec sponsor and as a polished emailed summary for the customer exec. Keep it tight, measurable, and action-oriented.

Use cases (how to use):
- Pre-read for a 1:1 sponsor call (send 24–48 hours ahead).
- Attach as the top of a QBR deck to orient executives.
- Convert to an email body for external recaps.

TL;DR (one-line):
- Redwood delivered predictable latency and 7% unit cost reduction this quarter; customer experiments on Dedicated saw 2x throughput for search use-case. Renewal pulse: on-track (no red flags) but need exec support for broader license upsell.

Key outcomes (metrics + context):
- Performance: 99th percentile latency for primary generation route is 180ms (target 200ms) — stable week-over-week.
- Cost: Token unit cost down 7% after batching and cache changes (see linked PR: JIRA CS-7742).
- Uptime: 99.93% platform SLA for hosted endpoints during quarter; two short region failovers (both auto-healed).
- Product impact: Search relevance experiment (A→B) improved MRR-led conversions by estimated 3.1% (internal evals).
- Adoption: 8 teams active (up from 6); 24 routes instrumented for tracing.

Customer health signal summary (quick view):
- Usage trend: steady growth (+12% q/q) concentrated in night batch windows.
- Engagement: Weekly technical syncs with infra and product teams; Solutions SE landed two integrations.
- Satisfaction: NPS snapshot (internal poll): +18 (sample n=34).

Risks & open issues (askable items):
1) Capacity predictability: Dedicated pool is fine for current load but customer expects a guaranteed burst plan for Black Friday-like events — ask: executive alignment to approve 1.5x reserved burst for 3 months.
2) Compliance audit: Customer requested a stronger audit trail for private deployment (KMS key rotation logs). Engineering estimates ~3 weeks to deliver hardened logs.
3) Cost transparency: Customer finance team wants monthly breakdown by route — propose a 3-month trial of Redwood Console premium retention for detailed billing.

Renewal pulse & timeline (what we want):
- Renewal target: 2026-07-15 (annual).
- Current likelihood: Green (70–80%) if we deliver: (a) burst capacity plan, (b) compliance audit artifacts, (c) clear cost transparency demo to finance.
- Exec ask: Sponsor help to unblock procurement and align procurement & security calendars.

Top 3 asks for executive sponsor (exact language to use):
1) "Can you confirm budget lane for a temporary capacity reservation to cover expected peak events next quarter?"
2) "Can your security lead allocate an hour this month to align on KMS rotation/attestation expectations?"
3) "Would you be willing to join a 15-minute procurement sync with our Sales Ops to accelerate contract signature?"

Suggested action plan (next 30 days):
- Week 1: Send pre-read + roster for 15-min sponsor call.
- Week 2: Demo Console premium billing view to customer finance (30 min).
- Week 3: Deliver audit artifact outline and target dates (SRE + Security).
- Week 4: Finalize proposal for 1.5x burst; capture sponsor approval and procurement timeline.

Owner & contacts (quick):
- CSM (owner): Aisha Patel (aisha@redwood.ai)
- Solutions SE: Lucas Morgan (lmorgan@redwood.ai)
- Account Exec: Priya Desai (priya@redwood.ai)
- Eng lead (compliance): Jordan Lee (jordan@redwood.ai)

Customer one-paragraph summary (copy for email):
Hi <SponsorName>,

Quick update from Redwood for Q1: We reduced per-token cost by ~7% from optimized batching and caching, maintained sub-200ms p99 latency on your primary generation route, and saw a measurable lift in search-to-activation in the A/B experiment. We recommend a short approval to enable temporary burst capacity and a quick compliance sync to finalize audit artifacts before your renewal in July.

Suggested short email subject lines (pick one):
- Q1 Outcomes + Quick Approval Request
- Redwood Update: Cost, Performance, Renewal Pulse
- 10-minute sponsor sync: burst capacity + audit artifacts

Speaker notes / call flow (for CSM):
0–2 min: Thank sponsor, highlight high-level metric (p99 latency + cost delta).
2–6 min: One slide each for Performance, Cost, Adoption (keep numbers crisp).
6–10 min: Risks & asks — make the three asks, be explicit about who we need from their side.
10–12 min: Close — next steps and proposed meeting times.

Attachments & prep (what to send with pre-read):
- Short CSV: monthly token usage and cost by route (generated by finance ops).
- One-pager: technical summary of Dedicated pool sizing and burst options.
- Audit checklist: KMS rotation and access logs requirements.

Notes to self / TODOs (internal):
- Confirm burst pricing with pricing ops (assigned: Priya).
- Get SRE ETA for audit logs (assigned: Jordan).
- Create Console billing demo account and schedule a demo slot with customer finance.
- Convert TL;DR into a slide and attach to pre-read.

Unresolved questions (for next sync):
- Does the customer consider temporary burst as a procurement or engineering cost? (Procurement likely but confirm.)
- Are there any internal blackout dates for procurement approvals before July?

Related links (quick):
- Confluence: CSR-portfolio-views (detailed health dashboard).
- JIRA: CS-7742 (cost optimizations epic).
- Slack thread: #cust-nyc-enterprise — recent notes on burst requests.

Version history / changelog (brief):
- 2026-02-25: created initial draft post-weekly health sync.
- 2026-03-03: added NPS snapshot and adoption numbers (Lucas).
- 2026-03-10: updated renewal pulse and refined asks (Priya).

Quick formatting checklist before send: 
- Replace <SponsorName> with actual sponsor name.
- Attach CSV + one-pager + audit checklist.
- Run subject line A/B test internally if multiple execs involved.

End of one-pager.

(Keep this file short and convert to a single-slide pre-read when ready; avoid adding full QBR decks into this doc — this is the 10-minute executive summary.)
